 Eligibility criteria


   ➢ A student must have secured minimum 50 marks (for Arts) and 55 marks (for science) in
      the concerned subject where he/she is willing to take Honours. (**The minimum qualifying
      marks for Mathematics Honours is 50).
   ➢ For Honours in Education, a student not having Education as a subject but Sociology or
      Psychology with minimum 50 marks can also apply.
   ➢ For Economics Honours (BA/BSc), a student of science stream should compulsorily pass
      in Mathematics.
   ➢ Students who are willing to change stream from Science to Arts/Commerce need to have
      standardized marks of 55 % or above.
   ➢ Students applying for Chemistry and Physics Honours need to necessarily pass in
      Mathematics.
   ➢ Students applying for Botany Honours need to necessarily pass in Chemistry.

             Guwahati College: A brief Introduction

               “Great works are performed not by strength but by perseverance.”


        Guwahati College situated in the eastern part of Guwahati is one of the premier institutions
  of Assam for higher learning in the region. It has a strength of nearly three thousand students,
  who are ably guided towards the achievement of their goals, by a highly qualified and
  experienced teaching community.
        The College was started on 3rd August 1964 at Chandmari, Guwahati. Later, it was shifted
  to its permanent building in Bamunimaidam at Jyotinagar. The College has now traversed
  through half a century, successfully contributing to the upliftment of the society. It is now one
  of the most reputed Colleges of Assam where students from all over the Northeastern Part of
  India get admitted.
        Guwahati College has completed 58 glorious years of existence and Reaccredited (Cycle
  2) by NAAC with Grade B with a CGPA of 2.62 in 2015. The College now stands as a full-
  fledged Institution of higher learning equipped with the latest educational technology. The
  infrastructure reflects the development of the College with its well-stocked library,
  Departmental Libraries, Seminar Halls, well equipped Laboratories, and a beautiful playground.
        The College has its own unique Anthem. At present the College has three streams both in
  H.S. and Degree level. Today the College provides honours courses in sixteen subjects. The
  Government of India under DBT provided an Institutional Biotech Hub in the year 2011 for the
  benefit of students and teachers.

  The Mission of the College:

        The mission of the College is to transform the society through spread of knowledge,
  education of the youth and development of personality, acquisition of skills by learners, creation
  of dedicated human resources, and helping in Nation Building.
  The Vision of the College:

        Guwahati College dreams to become one of the leading and pioneering institution in
  the society forimparting quality and value-based education. It emphasizes honesty, sincerity,
  hard work and dedication amongst the students by producing academically excellent students,
  as well as sensible and honest citizens.

    College Emblem:

        The College emblem with its motto is highly suggestive of the institution's mission and
  vision. In appearance, the emblem resembles a lotus in partial bloom. This highlights the
  Nationalistic spirit that prevails in college. It also suggests opportunity for the students to
  prosper. This image further emphasizes the optimistic spirit that forms the basis of the mission
  of the College -"the will to develop and improve further".
        The figure of the open book implies the propagation of education while the alternate dark
  and white lines suggest the College's endeavor to reach out to humanity in its entirety without
  any prejudice against caste, creed or colour. The earthen lamp, illuminating the surroundings to
  remove any darkness of ignorance, forms the motto of spreading the light of knowledge. The
  small dots represent the multitude that is expected to be benefitted by the propagation of
  knowledge.
Attendance Requirements:
   ➢ To be eligible to appear at a University Examination every student has to attend a minimum
       of two-third of the lectures, practical and tutorials held during the academic session.
   ➢ The principal shall have the power to strike off the name of a student who is grossly
       irregular in attendance.
   ➢ Students remaining absent on medical grounds should submit a medical certificate from
       the appropriate authority while rejoining college. However, absence on Medical Grounds
       does not mean that they will be exempted from any kind of examination.
Discipline:
The college expects its student to conduct themselves in a disciplined and dignified manner in the
college and outside. Students must follow the following rules:
   1. Students are responsible for their conduct and are prohibited from doing anything, either

  2. Interference of any outside pressure group in the internal affairs of the college is strictly

  3. Students are expected to have regard and consideration for each other and be respectful to

  4. Unbecoming language or ungentlemanly conduct shall be severely dealt with.

     and must keep as quiet as possible at all times. During their free periods students should
     work quietly in the Library or Reading Room, or spend the time in the Students Common
     Room, but without causing any disturbance.
  6. Students shall take proper care of the college property, furniture and premises. They must
     not cause damage to or tamper with college property, furniture and fittings.
  7. Students shall leave their bicycles, scooters or motorcycles locked in the parking shed
     provided for this purpose. No bicycle, scooter or motorcycle shall be parked in any other
     part of the college campus.
  8. No society can be formed in the college nor shall any person be invited to address a meeting
     in the college without the permission of the Principal.
  9. Notices designed to be pasted or circulated by the students anywhere in the college
     premises shall require the approval of the Principal.
  10. Students shall not spoil or misuse the lawns or any other space of the college.
  11. Communal harmony must be maintained.
  12. Students suffering from any contagious or infectious diseases will not be permitted to

  13. It is mandatory for students to come to college in proper College uniform during class days

  14. Smoking, chewing tobacco and spitting betel-nut inside the college campus is prohibited.
  15. Students shall not loiter around in college uniform outside the college campus.

Ragging
Ragging in any form is strictly prohibited within the college premises or outside the campus.
Ragging ordinarily means any act, conduct or practice by which dominant power or status of senior
students is brought to bear on students freshly enrolled or students who are in any way considered
junior or inferior by other students. It includes individual or collective acts or practice which;
   ➢ Involve physical assault or threat or use of physical force.
   ➢ Violate the status, dignity and honour of women students.
   ➢ Expose students to ridicule and contempt and affect their self-esteem.
   ➢ Entail verbal abuse and aggression, indecent gestures and obscene behaviour.
Any individual or collective act or practice of ragging and indiscipline shall be dealt with severely.
An anti-ragging committee as per UGC guidelines exists in the college.
Monitoring Academic Progress
The Principal, Teachers and IQAC of the college will meet the students on convenient dates during
the academic session to make firsthand assessment of academic progress or any problems related
to teaching and learning.
Guardians Meet
There will be specified meeting of the guardians with the Principal and teachers. Guardians should
attend such meetings to express their opinions on academic and other developmental matters of
their wards.

                                  Facilities And Features

 1. Identity Card

An Identity Card will be issued to every student at the time of admission. The card displays the
name, class, roll number and a recent passport size photograph of the student duly endorsed by the
college authority. Students are to carry their Identity Cards at all times. He / she will have to
produce the same whenever required to do so. Every student is required to get his / her identity
card renewed at the beginning of the new academic session. The identity card must be surrendered
at the time of leaving college.

 2. Academic Calendar and class schedule
Academic calendar is available in the college website. Time table will be available during the
commencement of the new session.
 3. Travelling Concession

Students are entitled to Railway/Air concessions to and from their homes during vacation and for
travelling on academic tours organized by the college.

 4. Students Aid Fund
The college has instituted a student’s aid fund. The objectives of the fund are:


         (a)   To render financial assistance to the economically backward and deserving
               students whose father’s /guardian’s income falls below BPL norms of the
               Government.
         (b)   To meet any other need of the students considered to be genuine by the college
               authority. A student requiring financial aid shall have to apply to the Principal of
               the college with an income certificate given by competent authority.

 5. Students’ Association and Co-curricular Activities

Guwahati College Students’ Union society is the general body of the students of this college. Every
student of the college is a member of this Society. The office bearers of the union are elected
annually. The Union endeavors to promote fraternity, mutual understanding, a sense of
responsibility among the students and works for all round development of the college. The Union
also organizes games and sports, debating, cultural activities among the students, under the
guidance of the teachers and the college authority.

teachers, students and office staff and reviews of educational, cultural, social and sports activities
of the college. The magazine is edited by a student editor under the supervision of a member of
the teaching staff. The college also publishes an annual News Bulletin.
   7. Library

The College has a well-stocked library. The library is open from 9:00 a.m. to 5 p.m. on all days
except Sundays and holidays. Students can borrow books from the library for two weeks. The
library is well equippedwith Xerox machines, internet facility and airy and spacious reading rooms
for teachers and students. SOUL 2.0, N-List (INFLIBNET) is available in the library. The library
subscribes to a large number of dailies, weeklies, periodicals and journals on a variety of subjects.
The library has a Book Bank for lending textbooks to deserving and needy students for one year.
Membership to the library, issue/return of books and searching/Referencing of books, all these
information can be obtained from the Librarian. Books on loan with members can be recalled at
any time without assigning any reason. Books kept in the reserve section are not issued on loan.

  8.   College Notice Board

All-important notice and information to students are displayed on the Notice Board. Students are
advised to see the Notice Board regularly.

 9. Examination

The college holds two Terminal/Sessional Examinations. These tests are intended to evaluate the
knowledge of the students and make them familiar with the examination system. All students are
required to appear in the Terminal/Sessional examinations. The final examination conducted by
the A.H.S.E.C. and G.U. are held in the college under the supervision of the Examination
Committee.

Guwahati College has a Career Counselling Cell. The Cell’s objective is to help students of the

training is imparted throughout the year by trained N.C.C. officers. There are many award and
scholarship schemes for eligible cadets including Vir Chilarai Award, Sahara Scholarship etc. It is
worth mentioning that NCC ‘C’ Certificate holders have various opportunities for Govt. services

exchange programme, community development, personality development, adventure training and
shooting are being taught to the cadets in the regular Sunday classes in the college premises.

commencement of the academic session.

services. Under this scheme the college unit has shown its proficiency not only in the State or

to join the N.S.S. can contact the respective Programme Officer after the commencement of the
academic session.
